# Artifact Completeness Model

**AI-generated by:** Alson (A.I Agent)

This model defines the states and dimensions used to assess how complete an existing or needed artifact is.

## Completeness States

| State | Definition | Example |
|-------|------------|---------|
| Not assessed | No evaluation has been performed | First pass, artifact not yet reviewed |
| Missing | The artifact does not exist in any form | No schedule baseline was created |
| Draft | Exists but not reviewed or approved | An unapproved project charter |
| Partial | Exists with some content, gaps remain | Risk register with risks identified but no responses defined |
| Complete | Contains all required content for its context | A fully approved and populated stakeholder register |
| Current | Complete and reflects the present state of the project | Most recent schedule baseline with approved changes |
| Outdated | Was once complete but no longer reflects current state | A budget baseline from before a reforecast |
| Combined | Content exists within a different artifact | Requirements defined in a contract instead of a requirements document |
| Not applicable | The artifact is not relevant to this project context | A detailed WBS for a fixed-price vendor delivery |

## Completeness Dimensions

Use these dimensions to determine whether an artifact is complete enough for its purpose.

| Dimension | Questions to Ask |
|-----------|------------------|
| Purpose | Does the artifact state its purpose? Is it clear what decision or activity it supports? |
| Contents | Are all expected sections or fields populated? Are there placeholders or pending items? |
| Owner | Is an owner or responsible party identified? |
| Approval | Is there evidence of review and approval? Who approved it and when? |
| Currency | Does the artifact reflect the current project state? When was it last updated? |
| Consistency | Is the artifact internally consistent? Does it conflict with other artifacts? |
| Traceability | Can the content be traced to its source (authorization, analysis, decision)? |
| Usability | Can a new team member understand and act on the artifact without clarification? |
| Lifecycle stage | Does the artifact match the current project phase? Is it premature or overdue? |

## Assessment Scale

| Score | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| 0 | Not addressed at all |
| 1 | Addressed but insufficient for use (placeholder, vague, or wrong) |
| 2 | Adequate for its current purpose with minor gaps |
| 3 | Fully meets needs for its context |
| 4 | Exceeds expectations, serves as a reference-quality example |

## Minimum Viable Definitions

When the disposition is `Create` or `Update`, the prescription must specify the minimum contents that make the artifact usable. These will vary by project size and context. General guidance:

| Project Size | What Minimum Contents Means |
|--------------|----------------------------|
| Small | The essential information needed to make the next decision. One page or less where possible. |
| Medium | Enough detail for a person familiar with the project to act without asking clarifying questions. |
| Large | Enough detail for a person new to the project to understand and act. Include cross-references to related artifacts. |
